'''Loran Donald Shields''' (born September 18, 1936) is an American academic. He was the president of [[California State University, Fullerton]] from 1971 to 1980, and of [[Southern Methodist University]] from 1980 to 1986.

==Early life and education==
Loran Donald Shields was born on September 18, 1936, in [[San Diego, California]].<ref name="libtexas">{{cite web|url=http://www.lib.utexas.edu/taro/smu/00114/00114-P.html|title=L. Donald Shields papers A Guide to the Collection|website=www.lib.utexas.edu}}</ref> He received a [[Bachelor of Arts|B.A.]] in chemistry from the [[University of California, Riverside]], and a [[PhD]] from the [[University of California at Los Angeles]] in 1964.<ref name="libtexas"/>

==Career==
From 1963 to 1967, he taught in the chemistry department at California State University, Fullerton, at which time he became vice-president for administration.<ref name="libtexas" /><ref name="Graaf2009">{{cite book|author1-link=Lawrence B. de Graaf|author=Lawrence Brooks De Graaf|title=The Fullerton Way: 50 Years of Memories at California State University, Fullerton|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=VJhVPgAACAAJ|access-date=23 December 2011|date=May 2009|publisher=The Center for Oral and Public History California State University, Fullerton|location=800 No. State College Blvd., Fullerton, CA 92834|isbn=978-0-930046-26-2|page=125}}</ref>  At the time of his appointment to the presidency of California State University, Fullerton in 1971, he was the youngest president of a public college or university in the United States.<ref name="libtexas" />

He served as the president of [[California State University, Fullerton]] from 1971 to 1980, until he took on the presidency of [[Southern Methodist University]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.calstate.edu/bot/leadership.shtml|title=Past & Present Leadership|website=www.calstate.edu|access-date=2010-05-01|archive-date=2016-07-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160717025717/http://www.calstate.edu/BOT/leadership.shtml|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.titanmag.com/2007/milestones/index.html|title=TitanMag.com|website=www.titanmag.com}}</ref> He resigned in 1986 because of health issues, at the time of the [[Southern Methodist University football scandal]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dallasnews.com/sharedcontent/dws/spe/2004/feb25football/smu.html|title=One of world's oldest Christmas cards at Bridwell library|date=14 December 2009|publisher=}}</ref>

In 1974, President [[Gerald Ford]] appointed him to the [[National Science Board]].<ref name="libtexas"/>  He served on the [[National Science Board]] from 1974 to 1980.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nsf.gov/nsb/members/former.jsp|title=National Science Board|website=National Science Board}}</ref>  In 1989, he became the executive director of the [[California Council on Science and Technology]], and remained in that position until 1995.<ref name="libtexas"/> He also served on the board of the [[Research Corporation]] for Science Advancement from 1983 to 1986, and on the National Commission for [[Cooperative Education]].<ref name="libtexas"/>
